compliance_deadlines: 2025-08-02: Obligations for providers of GPAI models enter into application; providers of GPAI models placed on the market after this date must comply and systemic-risk model providers must notify the AI Office.
2026-08-02: European Commission enforcement powers for GPAI model provider obligations enter into application, including fines.
2027-08-02: Providers of GPAI models placed on the market before 2 August 2025 must comply.
policy_extraction.penalties_summary: From 2 August 2026, the European Commission's enforcement powers enter into application to enforce compliance with GPAI model provider obligations, including with fines.
policy_extraction.implementation_notes: Official European Commission policy webpage (last updated 2026-03-26) summarizing the non-binding Guidelines for providers of general-purpose AI models under the EU AI Act. Although not legally binding, the guidelines reflect the Commission's interpretation of key terms (such as general-purpose criteria, significant modifications, and open-source exemptions) and guide enforcement alongside the voluntary GPAI Code of Practice. Providers (or their authorised representatives) must use the EU SEND platform to submit notifications, reassessment requests, serious incident reports, and compliance reports to the AI Office.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: Innovation enablement is the dominant frame because the document repeatedly justifies the GPAI provider guidelines as a pragmatic, clear compliance tool designed to lower regulatory friction, clarify open-source exemptions, and help ecosystem actors 'innovate with confidence' and 'innovate with clarity and confidence.' Consumer and public safety, fundamental rights, and economic competitiveness appear as secondary frames in the concluding 'Big Picture' statement—which links the EU's AI approach to 'boosting research and industrial capacity while ensuring safety and fundamental rights'—as well as brief procedural references to systemic risks and serious incident reporting, but they receive far less explicit justification emphasis than enabling trustworthy innovation.
